body:
## Summary

`start` reconstructs the command to run by joining `argv` with a single space (`args-parser.js:244`, `command: commandArgs.join(' ')`) and hands the result to `bash -c`. All argument boundaries and quoting are lost, so any argument containing shell metacharacters is **re-parsed by the inner shell** as if the user had never quoted it.

```
$ node -e "console.log('hi')"
/bin/bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `('
/bin/bash: -c: line 1: `node -e console.log('hi')'
exit 2
```

The faithful argv is available three lines away — `rawCommand: commandArgs` is returned by the same function — but is **never read anywhere in the codebase**:

```
$ grep -rn "rawCommand" src/
src/lib/args-parser.js:166: * @returns {{wrapperOptions: object, command: string, rawCommand: string[]}}
src/lib/args-parser.js:245:    rawCommand: commandArgs,
```

## Reproduction

`start-command` 0.32.1 (latest), Linux, Docker 29.6.0.

**A — quoting is dropped (no isolation):**

```bash
$ node -e "console.log('hi')"
# expected: hi
# actual:   /bin/bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `('   (exit 2)
```

**B — same under docker isolation:**

```bash
$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- node -e "console.log('hi')"
```
log:
```
Command: node -e console.log('hi')
bash: syntax error near unexpected token `('
Docker container "docker-…" exited with code 2
Exit Code: 2
```

**C — argument boundaries are lost even without metacharacters:**

```bash
$ echo "a  b"                                        # direct
$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- echo "a  b"   # docker isolation
```
both log:
```
Command: echo a  b
a b            <-- the two spaces the user quoted became one
```
`echo "a  b"` must print `a␣␣b`. The word was re-split by the inner shell.

**D — the #91 repair covers the isolation paths but not the direct path:**

```bash
$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- bash -c "echo hello world"
#   log: hello world                     <- correct
$ bash -c "echo hello world"
#   prints an empty line, exit 0         <- ran `bash -c echo hello world`,
#                                           so $0=hello, $1=world and echo got nothing
```

Same for `$ bash -c "echo \$((1+1))"`: empty instead of `2`. `isShellInvocationWithArgs` / `buildShellWithArgsCmdArgs` are only reached from the isolation code paths, so in the **default, non-isolated mode** the behaviour #91 fixed is still present — silently now (exit 0, wrong output) rather than as a syntax error.

## Root cause

`src/lib/args-parser.js:237-246`:

```js
commandArgs = args.slice(i);
...
return {
  wrapperOptions,
  command: commandArgs.join(' '),   // <-- argv boundaries and quoting destroyed here
  rawCommand: commandArgs,          // <-- correct value, never consumed
};
```

Everything downstream (`isolation.js`, `screen-isolation.js`, direct execution) then consumes the flattened `command` string.

`src/lib/shell-utils.js` shows the problem was already met once: `buildShellWithArgsCmdArgs` is documented as *"everything after `-c` is one argument (**reverses `commandArgs.join(' ')`**)"* — a targeted un-flattening added for #91 (`bash -i -c "nvm --version"`). It repairs the one shape it knows about (`<shell> -c …`); every other command with a quoted argument is still flattened. `node -e`, `python -c`, `sh -c` nested deeper, `git commit -m "msg with spaces"`, `grep "a b"`, `jq '.a|.b'` are all affected.

## Suggested fix (code)

The single-vs-multiple argv distinction is enough to disambiguate, and it matches how the tool is already documented and used:

- `argv.length === 1` — the user quoted a whole shell script (`$ "ls | grep x"`). Pass it through verbatim, as today.
- `argv.length > 1` — the outer shell already did the splitting; each element is one argument. Shell-quote each element before joining, so the inner shell reproduces exactly the argv the user typed.

```js
// isolation-log-utils.js already exports shellQuote()
const { shellQuote } = require('./isolation-log-utils');

const command =
  commandArgs.length > 1
    ? commandArgs.map(shellQuote).join(' ')
    : (commandArgs[0] ?? '');
```

This generalises `buildShellWithArgsCmdArgs` (which could then be retired along with its "reverses `commandArgs.join(' ')`" comment) and makes `rawCommand` the single source of truth.

Trade-off, stated plainly: a user who today writes `$ echo a '&&' echo b` — deliberately escaping an operator so the *inner* shell runs it — would get a literal `&&` after this change. That form is already fragile (it depends on the flattening bug), and the documented way to pass a shell script is a single quoted argument (`$ "echo a && echo b"`), which keeps working unchanged. If that behaviour needs preserving, gate the quoting behind an opt-out (`--no-quote-args`) rather than leaving the default lossy.

Suggested regression tests:

```js
// argv boundaries survive the round-trip
expect(run(['echo', 'a  b']).stdout).toBe('a  b\n');
expect(run(['node', '-e', "console.log('hi')"]).stdout).toBe('hi\n');
expect(run(['bash', '-c', 'echo $((1+1))']).stdout).toBe('2\n');   // #91 stays fixed
expect(run(['ls | wc -l']).exitCode).toBe(0);                       // single-arg script form
```

## Workaround

Base64-encode the payload so it contains no metacharacters:

```bash
B64=$(base64 -w0 script.mjs)
$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- bash -c "echo $B64 | base64 -d > /tmp/s.mjs; node /tmp/s.mjs"
```

(The `bash -c` form survives only because of the #91 special case.)

## Related

- #91 (`bash -i -c "nvm --version"` was interpreted as `bash -i -c nvm --version`) — same root cause, fixed for one command shape only
- #84 (avoid `bash` inside `bash`)
title: Command argv is flattened with join(' '), so quoted arguments are re-parsed by the inner shell (`$ node -e "console.log('hi')"` fails)
